Digital subtraction angiography.title: Digital subtraction angiography
Digital subtraction angiography.technique:
Under strict aseptic condition USG and fluoroscopy guidance, Right CFA access taken with 18 G needle and 5 F sheath placed.

With the help of 5 Fr AR catheter, right CCA run were performed in AP and lateral views which revealed no significant abnormal blush. With the help of 5 Fr AR catheter, left ICA and ECA run were performed in AP and lateral views which revealed tumoral blush arising from cavernous segment of ICA and branches of internal maxillary artery and ascending pharyngeal artery (ECA).

The patient tolerated the procedure well. Femoral sheath removed and manual compression bandage applied. During Procedure 2500 units of heparin given. No intraprocedural/ immediate post procedural complications seen.
Digital subtraction angiography.post_op_plan:
Complete bed rest with right leg extended for 8 hours
Check right groin for bleeding/Hematoma; neurovascular exam and vital monitoring every 15 minx4, then every 30 min x2 then every 1 hx2

Glue embolization.title: Glue embolization
Glue embolization.clinical_profile: c/o swelling over right cheek, post op
Glue embolization.technique:
Under strict aseptic condition under USG and fluoro guidance, right CFA access taken. Access was obtained with 18 G needle and 5 F sheath placed.  2500 units of heparin administered

With the help of AR , left CCA cannulated and angiogram taken which revealed a nidus in the midline face along with early draining veins. Left ICA angiogram was unremarkable. Left ECA angiogram revealed the nidus to be supplied by branches of facial artery. These were cannulated superselectively with microcatheter  and embolized with glue emulsion. Post embolization angiogram revealed glue cast in the nidus with no contrast opacification/early draining veins.

With the help of AR , right CCA cannulated and angiogram taken which revealed a nidus in the right cheek and midline face along with early draining veins. Right ICA angiogram was unremarkable. Right ECA angiogram revealed the nidus to be supplied by branches of facial artery and internal maxiallry artery. These were cannulated superselectively with microcatheter  and embolized with glue emulsion. Post embolization angiogram revealed glue cast in the nidus with no contrast opacification/early draining veins.

No intra/ immediate post procedural complication were seen. Femoral sheath removed and manual compression bandage applied.
Glue embolization.post_op_plan:
Complete bed rest with left leg extended for 8 hours
Check right groin for bleeding/Hematoma; neurovascular exam and vital monitoring every 15 minx4, then every 30 min x2 then every 1 hx2

Glue and Coil Embolization.clinical_profile: Pancreatitis with splenic artery pseudo aneurysm
Glue and Coil Embolization.technique:
Under strict aseptic condition under USG and fluoro guidance, Right CFA access taken with 18 G needle and 5 F sheath placed.

With the help of C1 catheter, celiac trunk cannulated and angiogram taken which revealed a pseudoaneurysm arising from splenic artery. Access taken distally into the splenic artery and distal embolization done with multiple microcoils. Embolisation of the sac and neck done using glue emulsion.

Check angiogram & USG revealed no flow in the pseudoaneurysm.

No intra/ immediate post procedural complication were seen. Femoral sheath removed and manual compression bandage applied .During Procedure 2000 units of heparin given.
Glue and Coil Embolization.post_op_plan:

Check right groin for bleeding/Hematoma; neurovascular exam and vital monitoring every 15 minx4, then every 30 min x2 then every 1 hx2
Encourage fluid intake and continue routine monitoring

COIL AND GLUE EMBOLIZATION.title: COIL AND GLUE EMBOLIZATION
COIL AND GLUE EMBOLIZATION.technique:
Under strict aseptic condition under USG and fluoro guidance, right CFV punctured and 5Fr sheath placed. . Using Cobra catheter and guidewire combination, left renal vein accessed. Venogram taken with valsalva revealed dilated left testicular vein along with opacification of the varicocele. Left testicular vein accessed, and using microcatheter, foam sclerotherapy done for the varicocele using polidocanol. Multiple microcoils of varying sizes used for embolisation of the caudal part of testicular vein at the level of pelvic rim. The mid and proximal testicular vein embolized with glue lipiodol combination. Check venogram with valsalva revealed no opacification of the distal testicular vein or varicocele.

Patient tolerated the procedure well. Mild extravasation noted at the level of L5-S1. Managed conservatively
COIL AND GLUE EMBOLIZATION.post_op_plan:
Complete bed rest for 4 hours
Vital monitoring every 15 minx4, then every 30 min x2 then every 1 hx2
Start fluid diet for first hour, regular diet thereafter
Resume diet and previous orders

PVA Embolization.title: PVA Embolization
PVA Embolization.clinical_profile: Hyper vascular mass in nasopharynx- JNA
PVA Embolization.technique:
The risk, benefits, alternatives of the procedure were explained and informed written consent was taken. Under strict aseptic condition USG and fluoroscopy guidance, Right CFA access taken with 18 G needle and 5 F sheath placed.

With the help of 5 Fr H1 catheter, left ICA and ECA run were performed in AP and lateral views. Tumor blush noted in the nasopharynx arising from branches of ECA. After superselective cannulation of IMA using microcatheter, embolisation of culprit branches done using 355-500 micron PVA particles. Post embolization left ECA run revealed mild tumoral blush from branches of ascending pharyngeal arteries. Attempt were made to super selectively cannulate the culprit artery, however due to excessive tortuosity the artery could not be cannulated. Approx. 80-90 % embolization of the tumor was achieved.

With the help of 5 Fr H1 catheter, right ICA and ECA run were performed in AP and lateral views which revealed no abnormal tumoral blush.

The patient tolerated the procedure well. Femoral sheath removed and manual compression bandage applied. During Procedure 3500 units of heparin given. No intraprocedural/ immediate post procedural complications seen.
PVA Embolization.post_op_plan:
Complete bed rest with right leg extended for 8 hours
Check right groin for bleeding/Hematoma; neurovascular exam and vital monitoring every 15 minx4, then every 30 min x2 then every 1 hx2

Central venoplasty.title: Central venoplasty
Central venoplasty.clinical_profile: Known case of chronic kidney disease with facial and right upper limb swelling
Central venoplasty.technique:
Interventional Radiology

Under strict aseptic condition under USG and fluoro guidance, Right CFV access taken with 18 G needle and 9 F sheath placed.

With the help of 5Fr Multipurpose catheter, right subclavian vein catheterized and venogram taken in AP view which revealed stenosis of the right subclavian vein, right brachiocephalic vein and right brachiocephalic vein-SVC junction.

The stenosis was crossed using help of guidewires and wire parked in the right subclavian vein. IV Heparin administered prior to dilation. Dilation of the narrowing was dilated using balloons of size (10x40mm, 12x40mm and 16x40mm) over stiff guidewire.  Post venoplasty, check angiogram revealed good flow across the stenosis and decreased in flow in the collaterals.

No intra/ immediate post procedural complication were seen. Femoral sheath removed and manual compression bandage applied .During Procedure 3500 units of heparin given.
Central venoplasty.post_op_plan:
Complete bed rest with right leg extended for 8 hours
Check left groin for bleeding/Hematoma; neurovascular exam and vital monitoring every 15 minx4, then every 30 min x2 then every 1 hx2

DSA and TJLB (Transjugular liver biopsy.title: DSA and TJLB (Transjugular liver biopsy )
DSA and TJLB (Transjugular liver biopsy.technique:
Under strict aseptic condition, right IJV punctured with 18 G needle and 10 Fr sheath placed. IVC and RHV cannulated with MPA and hydrophilic guide wire combination. Venogram taken to confirm positioning of the catheter in RHV. Wire exchanged with superstiff guidewire. 10 Fr long sheath placed. Venogram revealed good flow in the RHV. Using metallic cannula and sheath, biopsy gun placed in the RHV. Two cores taken from liver parenchyma in formalin.  Sample handed over to the relatives.

IJV sheath kept in place for further management/plasma exchange. Bandage applied. No intra/ immediate post procedural complication were seen.

1500 IU heparin was given during the procedure.

PTBD internalisation.clinical_profile: Extended Modified right heaptecetomy with RYHJ and PTBD in situ.
PTBD internalisation.technique:
Under aseptic precautions, cholangiogram done through existing Malecot cather which revealed stenosis at the anastomotic site. Access secured using guidewire. 8 Fr sheath placed. Narrowing crossed using multiple guide wire and catheter combination. 8 Fr Ring biliary catheter placed with distal end in jejunum.

Patient tolerated the procedure well. Sheath removed and bandage applied.
PTBD internalisation.post_op_plan:
Inj. Ceftriaxone 1gm BD
Inj. Pantoprazole 40mg OD
Inj. Ondansetron 2cc SOS
Inj. PCM/Tramadol in infusion SOS
IV Fluid 60ml/hr

PICC placement.title: PICC placement
PICC placement.clinical_profile: Ca left breast,  post op status, on chemotherapy
PICC placement.technique:
Right Basilic vein thrombosed. Right Cephalic vein very small in calibre. Hence decision taken to place PICC in brachial vein.

Under strict aseptic condition, under USG guidance, right brachial vein punctured in mid arm using 21 G needle. Wire parked in IVC. Peel away sheath placed. 5 Fr dual lumen PICC line placed with tip at RA SVC junction. Peel away sheath removed. Backflow checked for both lumen. Flushing done with heparinized saline. Dressing applied. Procedure uneventful.
PICC placement.post_op_plan:
Regular flushing as advised
Exercise for right upper limb
Follow up Doppler tomorrow morning

Bilateral Adrenal Venous sampling with A.title: Bilateral Adrenal Venous sampling with ACTH stimulation
Bilateral Adrenal Venous sampling with A.clinical_profile: Hypertension with hypokalaemia, primary hyperaldosteronism-? Conn’s syndrome.
Bilateral Adrenal Venous sampling with A.technique:
Interventional Radiology

Under strict aseptic condition, under USG and fluoro guidance, Right Femoral Vein access taken with 18 G needle and 5 F sheath placed. ACTH infusion was started 30 min prior to venous access.

With the help of Cobra catheter the ostium of a vein arising from the posterolateral aspect of the IVC at D 12 level cannulated, possibly right adrenal gland and sample taken with gravity assistance. The ostia of accessory hepatic vein and right renal vein were adjacent, however separate from the aforementioned vein. These were also cannulated and venography was done to rule out any drainage from the adrenal region. No sample taken from these veins

Subsequently, left renal vein was catheterized with cobra catheter and selective cannulation of the phrenicoadrenal trunk was done using microcatheter. Sample taken from the phrenicoadrenal trunk.

Sample also taken from the IVC caudal to origin of both renal veins; and cranial to the origin of the possible right adrenal vein.

No intra/ immediate post procedural complication were seen. Femoral sheath removed and manual compression bandage applied .During Procedure 2500 units of heparin given.
Bilateral Adrenal Venous sampling with A.post_op_plan:
Complete bed rest with right leg extended for 3 hours
Check right groin for bleeding/Hematoma; neurovascular exam and vital monitoring every 15 minx4, then every 30 min x2 then every 1 hx2
Resume diet and previous orders

Gel Foam Embolisation.title: Gel Foam Embolisation
Gel Foam Embolisation.clinical_profile: Acute liver failure with right posterior chest wall hematoma
Gel Foam Embolisation.technique:
Under strict aseptic condition under USG and fluoro guidance, right CFA access taken. Access was obtained with 18 G needle and 5F sheath placed.

With the help of C1 catheter, angiograms taken from right 8th-12th posterior intercostal arteries which revealed active contrast extravasation from right 9th posterior intercostal artery. Superselective angiogram of right posterior 9th intercostal artery performed using microcatheter and embolization done using gelfoam slurry. Post-embolization angiogram done which revealed no abnormal extravasation.

No intra/ immediate post procedural complication were seen. Femoral sheath removed and manual compression bandage applied .
Gel Foam Embolisation.post_op_plan:
Complete bed rest with right leg extended for 8 hours
Check right groin for bleeding/Hematoma; neurovascular exam and vital monitoring every 15 minx4, then every 30 min x2 then every 1 hx2
